# Document models

A document model is code in `document-models/<name>/`, where `<name>` is the kebab-cased model name. `ph generate document-model` writes a stub: a working model with one example module. You replace the example state and operations with the model's own, in the files the stub created. Nothing regenerates those files.

## Plan

In an interactive session, present the proposal and wait for approval before creating anything. Without a user, state the proposal and continue.

The proposal names:

- Type id: `<organization>/<document-type-name>`, e.g. `pizza-plaza/order`, `acme/invoice`.
- Extension: 2 to 4 characters with a leading dot, e.g. `.ordr`, `.inv`.
- Name: matches `/[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9 ]*/`, human-readable and capitalized, e.g. `"Order"`, `"Invoice"`. Spaces drop out of code names: `"Book List"` gives the folder `book-list` and the export `BookList`.
- The state schema, global and, if needed, local. See [references/state-schema.md](references/state-schema.md).
- Modules, each with its operations, their inputs and their errors.

Ask when the requirements are unclear. Split a complex model into modules of related operations.

### Design rules

- `global` scope: state shared among everyone with access to the document. `local` scope: state private to each user.
- One operation per user intent. Name operations for the intent, e.g. `addLineItem`, `updateRecipient`.
- Give every operation the errors its business rules need.
- Group related operations into a module.

## Create a document model

1. Run `ph generate document-model --name "<Name>" --code-first`. It writes `document-models/<name>/` and a starting editor in `editors/<name>-editor/`. The stub's type id is `<package name>/<name>`.
2. In `v1/definition.ts`, set the model's `id`, `extension`, `description` and `author`, and replace the example state: the object types, the `scopes.global.schema` and its `initialValue`. Add `scopes.local` when the model has local state.
3. Replace `v1/modules/items.ts` with the model's modules, one file per module, each declared with `<model>.module("<name>", { operations })`. List every module in `v1/index.ts`. See [references/reducers.md](references/reducers.md).
4. Replace the example tests in `v1/tests/` and run the checks. See [references/testing.md](references/testing.md).
5. Update the starting editor, which still dispatches the example operations. The powerhouse-editors skill covers it.

## Change a document model

Edit the declaration: state in `v<n>/definition.ts`, operations and reducers in `v<n>/modules/`. The action creators, types and stored schema derive from it, so there is one place to change.

After a state change, check every reducer and editor that reads or writes the changed fields.

A change that documents of the current version cannot load belongs in a new version: copy `v<n>/` to `v<n+1>/`, set `version` in its `definition.ts`, list the new version in the model's `index.ts` and in `upgrades/index.ts`, and add the transition from version n as `upgrades/v<n+1>.ts`. The comments in those files say what each expects.

## What the stub holds

| Path | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `document-models/<name>/index.ts` | The model's entry: every version as `<Name>V<n>`, and `<Name>`, the latest. Import `actions`, `reducer` and `utils` from one of them. |
| `v<n>/definition.ts` | Metadata, state types and initial state, declared with `defineDocumentModel` and the `ph` builders from `document-model`. |
| `v<n>/modules/<module>.ts` | A module's operations: each declares its input, its errors and its reducer. |
| `v<n>/index.ts` | The version: the definition with its modules. |
| `v<n>/tests/` | The version's tests. |
| `upgrades/index.ts` | The versions the model publishes and the upgrade into each one after the first. |

All of it is yours to edit.

### Models with a `<name>.json` and a `gen/` folder

A model directory that holds `<name>.json`, `gen/` and `src/reducers/` was written in the earlier, specification-based form. Its `gen/` folder is generated: never edit it. `ph generate document-model --dir <name>` regenerates it from the `.json`. To change such a model's state or operations, convert it first with `ph migrate --document-model <dir>`, then edit the declaration as above.

## Check your work

- `ph model check`: checks every model in the project. `tsc` cannot run these checks.
- `npm run tsc`
- `npm run lint:fix`
- `npm run test:coverage` after a reducer change. Reducers stay at 95% or more on lines, branches, functions and statements.
